modules.title: Traditional spacecraft 6-DoF and balanced reaction-wheel dynamics
modules.expensive_path: Repeated spacecraft equation-of-motion evaluation, coupled hub/wheel back-substitution and time integration. A single small trajectory may be too cheap to accelerate; no runtime or speedup has been measured. Workload significance must be established before a timed task is proposed.
modules.rationale: One coupled production dynamics module, with orbital translation, torque-free attitude and balanced wheel actuation as three experimental regimes of the same hub-centric state propagation. The scenarios are not three independent modules.
excluded: MuJoCo dynamics; docking/contact; flexible/slosh effectors; multi-spacecraft simulation
FSW controller performance, wheel voltage interfaces, imbalance/jitter and friction scenarios
SPICE-driven ephemerides and optional large-data downloads at runtime; the intact upstream payload is retained
A GPU port, Monte Carlo task, final check suite, tolerances and benchmark evidence are downstream work
hazards: Native source build attempted with Conan 2.28.1 on Windows CPython 3.12.14 but failed before compilation because no C++ compiler was detected; native examples/tests and timings remain unmeasured.
The upstream Conan recipe always requires CSPICE and CFITSIO, even with MuJoCo, visualization and optical navigation disabled.
Balanced-wheel locked inertia belongs in the configured spacecraft inertia; adding the Js*axis-projected body-rate term again would double count it.
Attitude must be compared as a rotation, accounting for MRP shadow sets; conservation alone also accepts frozen or wrong-frequency trajectories.
The complete source contains 3818 files totalling 326345194 bytes, including unused assets. Source review must distinguish retained payload from runtime dependencies.
The official reference is produced from pristine source at grading time; the supplied proposal restriction on fixed pre-generated fixtures must yield to that contract.
modules.purpose: One coupled production dynamics module, with orbital translation, torque-free attitude and balanced wheel actuation as three experimental regimes of the same hub-centric state propagation. The scenarios are not three independent modules.
primary_inputs: Initial position and velocity in SI units; central-body gravitational parameter
Initial MRP attitude and body rate; configured spacecraft inertia and mass
Balanced wheel spin axes, spin inertias and relative speeds; deterministic motor torque commands
primary_outputs: Time-stamped spacecraft position, velocity, MRP attitude and body angular rate
Energy and angular momentum diagnostic logs from spacecraft
algorithm_stages: Register hub states and link effectors through the dynamic parameter manager
Evaluate central point-mass acceleration and hub equations of motion
Accumulate balanced-wheel back-substitution matrices and motor-torque coupling
Integrate coupled spacecraft and wheel states, update attitude representation and publish messages
unique_responsibilities: Coupled balanced-wheel internal momentum exchange using the same spacecraft integration state
not_responsible_for: MuJoCo dynamics; docking/contact; flexible/slosh effectors; multi-spacecraft simulation
FSW controller performance, wheel voltage interfaces, imbalance/jitter and friction scenarios
SPICE-driven ephemerides and optional large-data downloads at runtime; the intact upstream payload is retained
A GPU port, Monte Carlo task, final check suite, tolerances and benchmark evidence are downstream work
modules.differences: One module spans the coupled hub and wheel equations; orbital, torque-free and wheel-actuated scenarios are regimes, not separate modules. Other Basilisk FSW, sensing and flexible/contact dynamics are retained in source but excluded from the initial proposal.

known_review_gaps: Native build failed before compilation because no C++ compiler was found; source-built scenarios and all timings remain unmeasured. The curator explicitly approved an early source-only Draft with this limitation visible.
No Docker execution, finalized task policy, official task verification or accelerator implementation is included.

The complete 326 MB payload includes optional assets and unrelated modules; the planned runtime does not use SPICE ephemerides or large-data downloads, but CSPICE and CFITSIO remain unconditional Conan dependencies.
The balanced-wheel momentum reconstruction is source-derived but has not been cross-checked experimentally against the upstream logger.
There is no measured evidence yet that a small single-wheel trajectory is a worthwhile timing workload.
open_questions: Which relevant upstream configurations provide a meaningful acceleration workload without expanding the agreed scientific scope?
Can a source build with the optional features disabled run the required examples without pulling large support data?
Which physical trajectory outputs and independent analytic/conservation checks should be finalized after native investigation and calibration?
